newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bildt to name supervisor for Bosnia town - sources.
newsitem.headline: Bildt to name supervisor for Bosnia town - sources.

text.p: Carl Bildt, the international community's High Representative to Bosnia, is expected to appoint an international supervisor on Friday for the disputed Bosnian town of Brcko, diplomats said.
"It is 99.9 percent certain it is going to be U.S. diplomat Robert Farrand," a diplomat, who asked not to be named, said.
The strategically vital port town of Brcko, on the Sava river on Bosnia's northern border, sits on a narrow land corridor which links the eastern and western halves of Serb-held territory.
It was seized early in the 1992-95 war by Bosnian Serbs who expelled its majority Moslem and Croat population.

Bosnia's 1995 peace agreement failed to resolve the Brcko issue, leaving it to international arbitrators who decided in Rome on February 14 to place the town under international supervision pending a final decision next year.
The Serbs say they are prepared to go to war again rather than lose Brcko, fearing their northern territory would be cut off.
The Moslems and Croats in turn claim Serb control over Brcko would reward so-called ethnic cleansing and deprive them of access to the Sava and Danube rivers and other main European waterways.
The arbitrators also decided to name a supervisor to deputise for Carl Bildt.
Bildt is expected formally to announce the choice of supervisor after a conference on implementation of the Brcko decision in Vienna on Friday.
Local newspapers in Sarajevo said Farrand is a career State Department diplomat with experience in eastern Europe.
If appointed, Farrand would be empowered to issue regulations to local police and to set up a multi-ethnic police force, according to the arbitration ruling.
The supervisor should also ensure full freedom of movement, oversee the return of Moslem and Croat refugees and implement an economic revitalisation programme for the Brcko area.
